title: Quantization noise regression bench + dynamic threshold scheduler for AWQ/GPTQ int8/int4
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a repeatable, high-resolution evaluation bench that quantifies the functional 'noise' (quality regressions) introduced by model quantization profiles (AWQ and GPTQ) at int8 and int4 levels and surface per-model+profile thresholds into the Console's alerting/rollout system. Goals: (1) produce stable metrics per workload type that correlate with real-customer regressions, (2) generate threshold recommendations for automated gating, and (3) implement a dynamic threshold scheduler that updates gates based on rolling historical variance and recent drift. This ticket covers data selection, metric design, bench implementation, and an integration spike to wire thresholds into the rollouts/alerts pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: A repeatable bench that runs nightly for a chosen model family (e.g., open-gpt-1 / o-gpt-1) and compares fp16 baseline vs AWQ/GPTQ int8 and int4 profiles

Bench produces these metrics per workload: mean embedding-cosine delta, stable-LL/ perplexity delta on held-out next-token, instruction-response semantic similarity (HumanEval-style scoring for code where applicable), and a calibrated composite quality score
Per-model+profile threshold recommendations computed (baseline + lower-bound) and stored in Console metadata API
Dynamic threshold scheduler prototype that recalculates alert thresholds using a 28-day rolling window and flags profiles when metric delta exceeds 3-sigma or an absolute threshold
Smoke integration: a rollout plan can be automatically blocked if a profile triggers the threshold; an alert is generated and linked to the regression bench run and failing prompts
PR with unit and integration tests merged and an internal doc describing methodology and limitations published to Confluence
investigation_notes: Early experiments (2026-02-15) showed embedding-cosine delta correlates better with human-perceived degradation than raw token-level perplexity for summarization and instruction tasks. AWQ-int8 tends to have low mean embedding delta (<0.02) for short prompts but shows long-tail failures on longer-context instruction prompts. GPTQ-int4 matched AWQ-int4 on average quality but exhibits higher variance across seeds. We need to track per-seed and per-batch variance and include per-layer sensitivity diagnostics for future gating heuristics.
experiment_results_summary: Nightly run #3 (2026-02-25) across 3 workloads: summaries (XSum-derived 1k prompts), chat-style instruction (Instruct-1000 synthetic), and code generation (HumanEval subset). Results vs fp16 baseline: AWQ-int8: embedding delta median 0.012, 95th pct 0.081; GPTQ-int8: median 0.014, 95th pct 0.092. AWQ-int4: median 0.045, 95th pct 0.36; GPTQ-int4: median 0.048, 95th pct 0.42. Composite quality score drop crossed provisional threshold for AWQ-int4 on code generation. Detailed per-prompt failing samples stored in Drive artifact.
test_plan:
1) Unit tests for metric computations (embedding cosine, normalized perplexity, and composite score).
2) End-to-end bench run on small subset in CI using a pinned model and synthetic prompts to validate stability.
3) Nightly full-run on dedicated infra (GPU pool with pinned seeds) with results written to s3 and Console metrics.
4) Manual verification of top-20 failing prompts per profile by a reviewer before turning on auto-blocking for that profile.
decisions: Metric set: use embedding cosine delta as primary signal + normalized token-level perplexity as secondary.
Composite score formula chosen: 0.7 * embedding_delta_norm + 0.3 * perp_delta_norm (both normalized to [0,1] using historical baselines).
Threshold policy: start with conservative absolute thresholds (embedding_delta > 0.05) and an adaptive 3-sigma rule based on 28-day rolling variance.
Alerting semantics: alert -> PagerDuty only for P0 regressions; otherwise create Console incident and send to #model-ops for triage.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: embedding delta may be dataset-dependent and miss semantic regression types. Mitigation: maintain per-workload thresholds and keep human review for initial 4 weeks.
Risk: false positives due to transient GPU nondeterminism. Mitigation: require failing sample rate > 0.5% and repeat the run with 3 different seeds before auto-blocking.
Risk: drifting baselines as models are updated. Mitigation: dynamic scheduler re-centers baselines monthly and logs baseline changes for audit.
